items.reason: Describes storing the SafeParse wrapper as Google's credential key instead of its parsed data, corrupting subsequent credential reads.
Describes computed Zod keys becoming literal property names rather than wildcards, breaking sync-mode token validation.
Describes passing the Bigin credential id where refreshOAuthTokens expects the user id, sending the wrong calcomUserId.
Includes the unconditional Salesforce token refresh and database write during connection setup. Refreshing only when needed fixes the golden issue.
Describes the webhook's non-constant-time secret comparison and its timing leak.
Describes persisting the SafeParse wrapper instead of token data as the Google credential key.
Describes passing credentialId instead of userId to Bigin's refreshOAuthTokens call.
Describes corrupting Google's stored credential by saving the SafeParse wrapper rather than its data.
Describes the literal computed property names in the minimum token schema that break sync-mode validation.
Describes sending Bigin's credential id as calcomUserId because the wrong third argument is passed.
Describes saving the SafeParse result wrapper as Google's credential key instead of the parsed payload.
Describes passing credentialId where userId is required, causing the sync endpoint to look up the wrong identity.
Describes the raw fetch Response returned in sync mode conflicting with Zoho CRM's expectation of an axios-style .data payload.
Describes using the credential row id instead of the user's id in Bigin's credential-sync request.
Describes misleading JSDoc that labels a credential type as an app slug. None of the golden issues concerns this documentation error.
Describes Bigin passing credential.id as the userId argument, requesting tokens for the wrong identity.
Includes persisting the SafeParse wrapper as credential.key, the same Google credential corruption identified by the golden issue.
